title: Provisional measurement review
notice: These are newly derived, unvalidated educational observations. The source supplies no printed answer key for this exercise. They are unscored and require qualified ECG educator review.

fields.value: Five dominant troughs; RR 230.5–241 px, approximately regular with mild variation.

fields.reason: Observed intervals: 233.5 px, 240 px, 230.5 px, 241 px. These describe this brief sample, not a validated rhythm classification.

fields.basis: Assumed course speed 25 mm/s; 76 grid lines enclose 75 small horizontal intervals across 1003 pixels.
fields.reason: Mean fiducial spacing 236.25 px gives 84.9 bpm. 4 complete intervals were retained. The strip has no verified speed label. This is interval-derived, not a six-second count.

fields.value: Candidate P-wave observation: Interior cycles show low rounded positive pre-complex lobes followed by small positive and dominant negative complexes. First atrial segment is incomplete at left boundary. Positive lobes repeat, but the transition to initial ventricular rise is broad.
fields.basis: Original PDF page 305; repeated-complex visual review and independent source comparison
fields.reason: Provisional visible-deflection description, not validated atrial identity, atrial origin, or a diagnosis. Qualified ECG educator review is outstanding.

fields.value: Approximately regular ventricular spacing over this short strip, with a conditional mean rate near 85 bpm and repeated P-like lobes before the interior complexes. Sinus origin is a hypothesis requiring confirmation that these are sinus P waves with a consistent 1:1 P-QRS relationship. Predominantly negative complexes alone do not identify the pacemaker or establish abnormal conduction.
fields.basis: New unvalidated educational synthesis of the original raster, accepted conditional measurements and course criteria; not a source-authored rhythm answer
fields.reason: Any named rhythm is a conditional teaching hypothesis, not an assigned diagnosis or scored answer. Rate and duration estimates assume course speed of 25 mm/s, not a verified strip speed. Candidate P identity, atrial origin and conduction remain unadjudicated. Qualified ECG educator review has not occurred.

limitations: New wave-field estimates remain provisional and unscored. Range width reflects uncertain endpoints and reader disagreement, not a validated diagnostic category. QT/QTc, calibrated amplitudes and clinical diagnosis are not established.
The exact original PDF was checked. The inspected waveforms are embedded rasters; larger rendering does not add samples. Expert interpretation may still improve unresolved component identification.

PR interval unresolved: Broad transition from candidate P tail into initial positive component and prolonged negative recovery produce competing onset/end landmarks; exploratory windows are not accepted interval annotations.

QRS duration unresolved: Broad transition from candidate P tail into initial positive component and prolonged negative recovery produce competing onset/end landmarks; exploratory windows are not accepted interval annotations.
P-wave identification, atrial origin and conduction relationship remain unadjudicated. Small preceding contours alone do not establish sinus rhythm.

The grid is rescaled differently in the horizontal and vertical directions. Only independently checked horizontal spacing is used for time. The 75-square span would be about three seconds only under the course timing assumption; no six-second duration is inferred.

Landmark picking allowance of about ±2 source pixels is illustrative. Sensitivity calculations perturb average grid pitch by ±0.15 pixels and interval length by ±4 pixels; they are not statistical confidence intervals and exclude unknown speed, resampling distortion and incorrect waveform identification.
Adjacent-spacing variation is raster/line-thickness scale; independent upper/lower bands agree within 1 px. No missing vertical line identified at chosen threshold.
First complex is near left border; its full preceding atrial segment is not available. It is retained for trough-to-trough intervals because the ventricular trough itself is complete.
